content: This medication, known by the brand names Kimyrsa and Orbactiv, is an antibiotic specifically used to treat serious bacterial infections of the skin. It is administered as a single dose by a healthcare professional. During the infusion, some patients may experience infusion reactions. If you notice symptoms such as flushing of the upper body, back or chest pain, chills, or shaking, inform your doctor immediately. Other potential side effects include nausea, vomiting, or headache. This medication is prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, in rare cases, it may cause a severe intestinal condition due to the bacteria Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after treatment has ended. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before using oritavancin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Share your complete medical history with your healthcare provider before starting this medication. Oritavancin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary, as it is unknown whether it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as blood clotting tests (e.g., PT/INR/aPTT), potentially causing false test results. If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) or a poison control center immediately. In the U.S., you can contact the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, your doctor may order lab tests, such as liver function tests, to monitor your condition. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. Storage instructions are not applicable for this medication, as it is administered by a healthcare professional. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
